title: The Land Will Not Hold You

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Keep all my decrees and laws and follow them, so that the land where I am bringing you to live may not vomit you out. You must not live according to the customs of the nations I am going to drive out before you. Because they did all these things, I abhorred them.'" - Lev 20:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here God gives His reason, and it is not what many assume.

He is not driving out the Canaanites because Israel is racially superior or divinely favoured in some automatic way. He is judging centuries of practices that destroyed people — including the child sacrifice this chapter opened with.

And notice the warning built into the same sentence: so that the land may not vomit you out. The same standard applies to Israel. There is no exemption for being God's chosen people. If they do what the nations did, the same thing will happen to them.

And it did. Centuries later, Israel was carried into exile for exactly these sins.

That should end any complacency in us. Being part of God's people has never been a licence. Judgement begins with God's household (1 Pet 4:17). Paul warned the Corinthians using Israel's failures as the case study: these things happened to them as examples... So, if you think you are standing firm, be careful that you don't fall! (1 Cor 10:11-12).

God's patience is enormous — He waited generations before judging Canaan. But patience is not indifference, and belonging to Him is not a shield for living any way we choose.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you assumed your standing with God exempts you from His standards?
2. What does it mean that God warned Israel with the same words He used about the nations?
3. Where do you need to take God's warnings more seriously?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from complacency. Thank You for Your patience, and let me never treat belonging to You as permission to live carelessly. Amen.
